title: Muskrat Brings Up the Earth
text:
In an Anishinaabe story, a great flood once covered the whole earth. Nanabozho, the spirit hero, floated on a log with the animals who had survived. There was no land anywhere, and they could not live on the water forever.

Nanabozho said that if someone could bring up a little earth from the bottom, he could make new land. The Loon, a fine diver, went first. He was gone a long time, but he came up gasping and empty. The Otter tried and failed. The Beaver, strong and proud, dove deep and stayed down longer than anyone, and he too came up with nothing, almost drowned.

Then the little Muskrat said he would try. Some of the bigger animals laughed. Muskrat dove anyway and was gone so long that they gave up hope. At last his body floated to the surface. He had died in the attempt, but in his small clenched paw was a lump of mud from the bottom.

The Turtle offered his back. Nanabozho spread the mud on the Turtle's shell, and it grew and grew until it became the land that some Anishinaabe still call Turtle Island. The animals honored Muskrat, and in many tellings Nanabozho breathed life back into him.
lesson: Persistence can matter more than size or reputation. Do not dismiss the quiet member who volunteers after the stars have failed.
people: Nanabozho, Loon, Otter, Beaver, Muskrat, Turtle
location: Great Lakes region (Canada and the United States)
source: Anishinaabe (Ojibwe) oral tradition, the earth diver story
caveat: The animals who try first and the ending differ between communities and tellers.
